items.title: JBS, Tyson Stocks Jump on U.S. Plans to Resume Mexican Cattle Imports
items.summary: Shares in JBS and Tyson Foods—two of the largest U.S. beef processors—soared Monday after the Department of Agriculture revealed plans to lift a more than yearlong ban on Mexican cattle imports.  Live cattle futures prices–the price meatpackers pay feedlots for their cattle–ticked down about 1.5% on Monday.  Shares of Tyson are up 7% today, while JBS stock surged 10%.
